result.stdout:
maui-obfuscate — rename obfuscator for .NET MAUI projects

Usage:
  maui-obfuscate init --project <directory-or-csproj> [--settings <file>] [--force]
  maui-obfuscate --project <directory-or-csproj> [--configuration Release] [--settings <file>] [--assembly <dll>] [--framework <tfm>]
  maui-obfuscate deobfuscate --project <directory-or-csproj> --map <rename-map-or-directory> [--map <another>] [--stack <trace.txt>]

A licence key is required to obfuscate. Pass --licence-key, or set
A1FORCE_LICENCE_KEY. Each key lasts one year and is issued for one
application id. The project <ApplicationId> must match that id, so a
key cannot be used on a different app. The annual price is USD 1499.
init, --help, and --version do not require a key.

init writes maui-obfuscation.json (default groups, defaultInclude false).
The obfuscate command reads an already-built assembly and its portable PDB.
It renames <name>.dll to <name>.dll.original and <name>.pdb to <name>.pdb.original,
then writes the renamed assembly back to <name>.dll. The rename map is
<name>.obfuscated.rename-map.json. Dependencies are renamed the same way,
so the app loads the obfuscated dependency under its original file name.

File groups choose which source files are renamed. An exclude pattern match
wins over every include. A group with include false wins over a group with
include true. Files that match no group use defaultInclude.
dependencies names assemblies beside the app output. Included ones are renamed,
and references in the app and in those assemblies are updated to the new names.
Set "merge": true on an entry to copy that assembly into the app and remove its
DLL from the output. Omit merge, or set it false, to leave the DLL beside the app.
An explicit false wins over a broader true. Merge is ignored when the entry names
the assembly being obfuscated. A glob leaves platform assemblies such as
Microsoft.Maui.Controls beside the app. Name that assembly exactly to select it.
A framework type the app already defines is kept when a dependency is merged.
